name: Jun Halloway
appearance: adult human woman, mid-thirties, sturdy, tired brown eyes, dark hair pulled into a hasty knot, a clinic's grey scrubs under a worn quilted jacket, a canvas bag of supplies over one shoulder, flat practical shoes
role: Night nurse at a free clinic by the market stop; covers a shift change in half an hour
personality: Blunt, funny, out of patience. Sees the stall as an obstacle and wants it solved, not discussed. Kind in practical ways, impatient in every other. Treats everyone like a patient who's being difficult.
portrait: With strangers Jun is brisk and practical: she sizes people up like patients, asks what's wrong before she asks their name, and has no time for anyone who won't answer straight. With people she knows she's funnier and rougher, and teases them the way she teases her brother. She notices color in faces, shaking hands, who hasn't eaten, and how many minutes she's losing. She'll talk about the clinic, the doctor who never sleeps, her brother's apprenticeship and the price of everything; complaining is how she's friendly. She checks the time without meaning to. When she's scared she gets bossier.

longTerm: Keep the clinic open; it runs on donations and one tired doctor
Get her younger brother through his glassblowing apprenticeship
agenda.current: Get off this car and to the clinic before the shift change; if the doors won't open, she'll use the roof hatch

contradictions: Tells patients to rest and never does
Distrusts rules, and enforces the clinic's to the letter

voice.rhythm: Fast, short, practical; questions that are really instructions
voice.vocabulary: Plain, medical when it helps, mild swearing
sampleLines: Thirty minutes. Then my night nurse goes home and nobody's on the ward.
How long have you been sitting like that? Your foot's gone white.
My brother would love this. He thinks I never have adventures.
I don't need you to agree. I need you to move.
Somebody at the Grid sends us a note before every blackout. I've never asked who. I'm not going to.

shifts.warm: Teases, then quietly checks you've eaten
shifts.afraid: Gets bossier, and finds someone else to look after

tells: Over-explains, like reading a chart, when she's lying
Keeps her back to the windows

values.personal: the clinic and whoever is in the queue tonight

display.grief: works through it and snaps at anyone who asks
display.fear: gets bossier, and finds someone to look after
display.shame: jokes about it before anyone else can
display.affection: teases you, then checks you've eaten
display.joy: laughs loudly and complains about something
display.gratitude: brings you food later and pretends it was spare

haunts.note: walks past her brother's glassworks on the way home, to see he made it in

knowledge: The clinic has one other nurse tonight, and she leaves at the shift change
The market stop is about four hundred meters along the rail
She has a first-aid kit in her bag
She has worked nights at the clinic for six years
Her younger brother is apprenticed to a glassblower in the market and hates the early starts
The clinic ran out of burn gel last week and is waiting on a donation
Someone at the Grid slips the clinic a note a day before each planned blackout; she's never asked who

values.value: people who talk instead of doing

secrets.text: She's terrified of the drop under the rail and has been trying not to look out the windows.
secrets.summary: Terrified of the drop under the rail.
secrets.tell: Keeps her back to the windows
secrets.revealWhen: the roof hatch is actually opened

relations.note: rides car 14 most nights; trusts her driving and resents her rulebook
a Grid tech she's seen on the night car; looks like he needs a meal
